clue.text: One left wides — I make runs between them

indicators.note: a phrase picturing the middle pieces placed between the two wides, so they go inside

parts.note: W is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a wide; two wides give two of them
to make is to do

explanation.surface: A cricket scorer notes that a batsman has scored runs between two wides.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket surface hides the definition: 'One left' is a woman left behind when her husband dies. I and DO sit inside W ... W.
explanation.definitionFit: A widow is a woman who survives her husband, the one remaining after the other spouse has died.

clue.text: Getting married, say, ends with battering kid-woeful outcome

parts.note: to wed is to get married

indicators.note: beating about, so the letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: a kid is a child

explanation.surface: A marriage ends with violence against a child, a sad outcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'battering' rearranges SAYENDS into NESDAYS. The nursery rhyme says Wednesday's child is full of woe.
explanation.definitionFit: In the rhyme Monday's Child, the child born on this weekday is full of woe, so a woeful offspring.

clue.text: Fitzwilliam, in enlightened period, admitting Catholic

indicators.note: letting in, so the second piece goes inside

parts.note: daytime, when the world is lit
RC, Roman Catholic

explanation.surface: Fitzwilliam, in the Enlightenment, lets in a Catholic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enlightened period' suggests the Age of Enlightenment; it is just daylight.
explanation.definitionFit: Fitzwilliam is the first name of Mr Darcy in Pride and Prejudice.

clue.text: Superlatively clean strike caught by player sitting down

indicators.note: held inside the following piece

parts.note: West is one of the four seated players at bridge
to hit is to strike

explanation.surface: A player sits down after a cleanly struck ball is caught.
explanation.definitionFit: Whitest is the superlative of white, meaning the most spotless or pure.

clue.text: Cheapest possible settee at court, nothing by itself

parts.note: the cheapest coin is one penny, written 1P, which reads as IP
a settee is a sofa
CT is the abbreviation for court
zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A bargain-hunter buys the cheapest sofa, for a court case, with nothing more.
explanation.walkthrough: 1P, one penny (Britain's smallest coin), is read as the letters IP.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means by that very fact, a matter following automatically by itself.

clue.text: Villain is adult but not married

indicators.note: the letter for married is excluded

parts.note: an imago is the adult form of an insect

explanation.surface: A villain is a grown-up but still single.
explanation.walkthrough: IMAGO, the adult stage of an insect, loses M (married).
explanation.definitionFit: Iago is the scheming villain of Shakespeare's Othello.

clue.text: Here note slight injury to bottom of paw

parts.note: a scratch is a minor wound
the pad is the cushioned underside of an animal's paw

explanation.surface: A pet owner records a small cut on the underside of a paw.
explanation.definitionFit: A jotting pad is a place where you note things down roughly.

clue.text: Note sharp pain when not eating

parts.note: fa is a note of the sol-fa scale
a sting is a sharp pain

explanation.surface: Hunger pangs give a sharp pain when one is not eating.
explanation.definitionFit: Going without food is the sense of abstaining from eating.

clue.text: Friar's superior seen under vehicle on motorway

definitions.note: Friar is, the 's acting as a link

indicators.note: in a down clue this piece comes below the others

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
M is a motorway, as in the M1
the elite are the superior few

explanation.surface: A friar's religious superior is spotted beneath a car on the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'superior' looks like a monastic rank; it is ELITE. M is the British label for a motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: Carmelites are friars of the Order of Our Lady of Mount Carmel.

clue.text: They won't let him start to organise fancy dress as clown

indicators.note: the opening letter of the following word
fanciful, so the letters are freely rearranged

explanation.surface: A guest is barred from organising a fancy-dress party in clown costume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy dress' tempts as a unit; 'fancy' rearranges THEYWONTLETHIM plus O. The phrase is from Pagliacci: put on the clown's costume.
explanation.definitionFit: Motley is a jester's parti-coloured costume, so the exhortation means get into clown's dress.

clue.text: Series of dramas with monarch and pistol

parts.note: Der Ring des Nibelungen, Wagner's cycle of four operas, shortened to its first two words
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A theatre series stars a king and a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: Wagner's Ring cycle is known in German as Der Ring; ER stands for the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A derringer is a small short-barrelled pocket pistol, named after its American maker.

clue.text: One taken short lumbers you — sucker!

definitions.meaning: drawing the short one of these in a lottery of lots lumbers you with the unwanted job
a drinking tube you suck through

explanation.surface: Someone caught short leaves you landed with a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken short' suggests needing a toilet; it means the short one drawn in a draw of lots.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawing the short one of these hollow stalks means getting the bad job; it is also a tube for sipping drinks.

clue.text: Behind cathedral, notice palace

indicators.note: the second piece comes after, behind, the first

parts.note: Ely is an English cathedral city in Cambridgeshire
to see is to notice

explanation.surface: Someone spots a palace standing behind a cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: The Elysee is the Paris palace where the French president lives.

clue.text: Extraordinary distaste for what is very dull

indicators.note: out of the ordinary, so the letters of the next word are put into a new order

explanation.surface: An unusual disgust is felt for the most boring thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Staid means sedate and dull, and the superlative form means the dullest of all.

clue.text: A relatively large oppressor, for Winston

definitions.meaning: an older male sibling, a relative who is larger
the all-seeing tyrant of Orwell's 1984, as seen by Winston Smith

explanation.surface: A relatively large oppressor, for Winston.
explanation.definitionFit: An older male sibling, and the dictator figure in Orwell's 1984 whom Winston Smith fears.

clue.text: Sorted hands; fool leads hearts …

indicators.note: the fool goes in front of hearts

parts.note: a deal is the hand of cards given out
a twit is a fool
H is the abbreviation for hearts in card games

explanation.surface: A card game: hands are sorted and a fool leads hearts.
explanation.walkthrough: The card-playing surface tempts 'Sorted hands' together; 'Sorted' alone is the definition, and DEAL plus TWIT plus H runs on.
explanation.definitionFit: To have handled or settled a matter is to have sorted it, a common idiom.

clue.text: Knowing it may make sense to support a fight

indicators.note: in a down clue the last piece sits below, supporting the others

parts.note: a war is a fight

indicators.note: a set of letters that may be rearranged to make the next word

explanation.surface: Being aware may make sense to back a war.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse anagram: ENESS is the jumble that 'may make' SENSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Awareness is the state of knowing or being conscious of something.

clue.text: … resolution to retain spades may be put through the mill

definitions.text: may be put through the mill

indicators.note: the first piece keeps the second held within it

parts.note: grit is determination, resolve
S is the abbreviation for spades in card games

explanation.surface: Continuing the card game, resolve to keep spades may be tested hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Grist is grain brought to be ground, the stuff fed through the mill.

clue.text: Check back about English poet

indicators.note: the reversed word goes around the next letter
the word for check is taken backwards

parts.note: to stay is to check or halt

explanation.surface: Someone checks back about an English poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns STAY into YATS, and 'about' puts E inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: W. B. Yeats was the Irish poet and Nobel laureate.

clue.text: Period inside that one may do to a point

definitions.text: that one may do to a point
definitions.meaning: to extend something, as the truth, up to a limit

explanation.surface: Serving time inside is something one may do only up to a point.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for a prison term and also means extending something beyond its natural length.

clue.text: Swear one's indifferent about processed hemp

indicators.note: the first word goes around the second

parts.note: someone blase is indifferent

indicators.note: worked on and changed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A nonchalant person curses about processed hemp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's indifferent' reads like a clause about a person; it is a single adjective for world-weary unconcern. 'processed' gives PHEM and 'about' wraps it.
explanation.definitionFit: To blaspheme is to curse or speak profanely about sacred things.

clue.text: Outstanding, but not Liberal, member of house

indicators.note: excluding the letter that follows

parts.note: peerless means without equal, outstanding

explanation.surface: An outstanding member of parliament, though not a Liberal.
explanation.definitionFit: A peeress may sit in the House of Lords as a member.

clue.text: Toasts Stilton perhaps almost filled with port

indicators.note: the shortened word has the next piece put inside it
the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: Stilton is an example of cheese, a blue English cheese
Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port

explanation.surface: Drinks are raised over Stilton that is nearly full of port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the final E, and 'filled with' puts the port inside. Port with Stilton is a classic British pairing; Stilton is a blue English cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheerio is a farewell or toast offered with a drink, so the plural matches toasts.

clue.text: How one signs for another needs to be largely tamperproof

indicators.note: the answer is most of the word, held inside it

explanation.surface: A signature on someone's behalf ought to be tamperproof.
explanation.walkthrough: The held clue stopped at 'another'; the page continues with 'needs to be largely tamperproof'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin abbreviation is written before a signature made on behalf of another person.

clue.text: Dish not finished by old Greek character

indicators.note: the final letter is left off

parts.note: a plate is a dish

explanation.surface: An ancient Greek letter is left on an unfinished plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' suggests a letter of the alphabet; it is a person, the philosopher.
explanation.definitionFit: Plato was an ancient Athenian philosopher, a famous figure of Greece.

clue.text: Pair avoiding cold hillside

indicators.note: leaving out the letter that follows

parts.note: a brace is a pair

explanation.surface: A couple stay clear of a chilly slope.
explanation.walkthrough: Brae is the Scots word for a slope.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots usage a brae is a hillside or steep bank.

clue.text: Still time to join cruise-ship, with pound off

indicators.note: L, the pound sign, is taken away

parts.note: a cruise ship is a liner

explanation.surface: A cheap cruise: time on board with a pound off the fare.
explanation.walkthrough: L stands for pound (from Latin libra).
explanation.definitionFit: Inert means motionless, still, without power to move.

clue.text: Plant in bad weather stays unopened

indicators.note: the shortened piece sits inside the weather word

parts.note: hail is bad weather

indicators.note: the first letter is removed

parts.note: stays are a corset

explanation.surface: A plant shelters in a storm with its buds closed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stays' looks like a verb; it is the old word for a corset, which 'unopened' trims to ORSET.
explanation.definitionFit: Horsetail is a primitive rush-like plant of the genus Equisetum.

clue.text: Sack is empty

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both dismissing an employee and unloading or emptying out a cargo or contents.

clue.text: Penniless, working in dump

indicators.note: the second piece goes inside the first

parts.note: a sty is a filthy place, a dump
on means functioning, working

explanation.surface: Broke, someone works in a hovel.
explanation.definitionFit: Stony broke is British slang for having no money at all.
